## 0) Preprocessing:

```{r}
#### 1) Read the tables with Stress, CP, IB and covariates:
raw_complete_IB_dataset= read.csv("../data/MIDUS_data_mediations_cleaned_correct.csv") # dataset already cleaned (All non-valid values where replaced by NA)

### 2) Read Inflammation-related gene expression datasets:
library(haven)
# MIDUS Refresher 1:
REF1_GE_infl=read_sav("../data/MR_P6_RNAGENE_N863_MRID_20200605.sav")

```


### a) Reverse the corresponding stress variables:

Some stress variables are coded in reverse. This ensures that all stressors are coded with low values meaning low stress levels and high values meaning high stress levels

```{r}
### 1) Reverse the stress variables whose levels go from 1 to 4:
str_1_4  <- c("A1SE11", "A1SE14F", "A1SE14H", "A1SE14I", "A1SE16F",  "A1SE16H", "A1SE16I", "A1SE17A", "A1SE17B", "A1SE17C",  "A1SE17D", "A1SE17E", "A1SE17F", "A1SE17G", "A1SE17H", "A1SE17I", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17K", "A1SE17L", "A1SE17M", "A1SE17N", "A1SE17O", "C1SJ4H", "C1SJ4J", "C1SJ8F", "C1SJ8H")

table(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1SE17D)

# Reverse mapping function for values 1 to 4:
reverse_values_1_4 <- function(x) {
  return(5 - x)
}
# Apply the function to each variable using a loop:
for (var in str_1_4) {
  raw_complete_IB_dataset[[var]] <- reverse_values_1_4(raw_complete_IB_dataset[[var]])
}

table(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1SE17D)


### 2) Reverse the stress variable whose levels go from 1 to 6:
table(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC3)
# Reverse mapping function for values 1 to 6:
reverse_values_1_5 <- function(x) {
  return(7 - x)
}
# Apply the function:
raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC3 <- reverse_values_1_5(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC3)
table(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC3)


# 3) Reverse the stress variable whose levels go from 1 to 2:
table(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC14)
# Define the reverse mapping function for values 1 and 2
reverse_values_1_2 <- function(x) {
  return(ifelse(x == 1, 2, ifelse(x == 2, 1, x)))
}
# Apply the function:
raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC14 <- reverse_values_1_2(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC14)
table(raw_complete_IB_dataset$A1PC14)
```



### b) Merge M3_GE_infl and REF1_GE_infl datasets: 

```{r}
# Extract column labels to know what each column means:
column_labels_REF1 <- sapply(REF1_GE_infl, attr, "label")
```

```{r}
# 1) Create a new dataset with the same columns from REF1:
# Convert all columns of dbl+lbl type to plain numeric:
library(dplyr)
REF1_GE_infl_num = REF1_GE_infl %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.labelled), as.numeric))
  # Handle the ID column:
  REF1_GE_infl_num$MRID = as.numeric(REF1_GE_infl_num$MRID)

# EXTRACT ONLY the individuals with GE available:
REF1_GE_infl_aval=REF1_GE_infl_num$RA6RAVAIL==1
REF1_GE_infl_num=REF1_GE_infl_num[REF1_GE_infl_aval, ]  

# Take the columns ID, plate number (covariate for gene expression), and all genes:
ref1_GE_new= REF1_GE_infl_num[, c(1, 3, 6:ncol(REF1_GE_infl_num))]
names(ref1_GE_new)

merged_GE_dataset = ref1_GE_new

```

### c) Merge both datasets (all_except_GE + GE data) to create a complete dataset:

```{r}
## Merge the two datasets on the MIDUSID column:
# Change the ID column name of GE dataset 
names(merged_GE_dataset)[1] <- "MIDUSID"
# Merge the datasets:
whole_dataset_all_genes <- merge(raw_complete_IB_dataset, merged_GE_dataset, by = "MIDUSID", all.x = TRUE)

#### Select only European ancestry individuals (white):
WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes=subset(whole_dataset_all_genes,C1PF7A==1)

```


```{r}
# Save this dataset "WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes" and use it to create the SUBSET B for GE mediations:
save(WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes, file = "../data/WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes.RData")

```


## 1) Creation of SUBSET for INFLAMMATION regressions (SUBSET A):

```{r}
# 1) List of all 50 stressors:
stress_all_vars = c("A1PC3", "A1PC14", "A1SE9", "A1SE11", "A1SE14C", "A1SE14D", "A1SE14E", "A1SE14F", "A1SE14G", "A1SE14H", "A1SE14I", "A1SE14J", "A1SE14K", "A1SE15", "A1SE16C", "A1SE16D", "A1SE16E", "A1SE16F", "A1SE16G", "A1SE16H", "A1SE16I", "A1SE16J", "A1SE16K", "A1SE17A", "A1SE17B", "A1SE17C", "A1SE17D", "A1SE17E", "A1SE17F", "A1SE17G", "A1SE17H", "A1SE17I", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17K", "A1SE17L", "A1SE17M", "A1SE17N", "A1SE17O", "C1SJ1", "C1SJ4A", "C1SJ4B", "C1SJ4C", "C1SJ4H", "C1SJ4J", "C1SJ5", "C1SJ8A", "C1SJ8B", "C1SJ8C", "C1SJ8F", "C1SJ8H")

# 2) List of IBs:
IBs <- c("C4BCRP", "C4BMSDIL6", "C4BFGN", "C4BSESEL", "C4BSICAM", "C4BMSDTNFa")

# 3) List the covariates (or common variables) used in all models:
common_vars <- c("MIDUSID", "C1PRSEX", "C1PRAGE", "C1PB1", "C1SBMI", "COHORT", "C1SA26F", "C1STINC", "C1PHHSIZE", "C1SA11T")

# 4) List of CF tasks:
CFs = c("C3TWLITU", "C3TDBS", "C3TCTFLU", "C3TNSTOT", "C3TBKTOT", "C3TSCGBA", "C3TEM", "C3TEF")

### Group all variables that are going to use in IB regressions and mediations:
all_vars=c(stress_all_vars, IBs, common_vars, CFs)
```


```{r}
####### 1) WHITE group:
subset_white_mediations= WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes[, all_vars]

# Count how many valid data each variable has:
non_na_counts = colSums(!is.na(subset_white_mediations))
non_na_counts 

# Count complete cases:
sum(complete.cases(subset_white_mediations))

```

**NOTE:** Although IBs are the columns with more NA values (~ 1200 valid values), the **complete cases** of this full dataset is only **~300 rows**!!! 
Therefore, I have to clean the data to get more complete cases. 


#### Cleaning dataset:

**Creating <16% missing - dataset**

```{r}
library(naniar)
library(dplyr)
# Visualize RAW dataset:
vis_miss(subset_white_mediations)

#######  Filter 1:
# Retain individuals with AT LEAST ONE non-missing inflammation biomarker value (it is the same that filter out individuals with all IB=NA values)
subset_white_mediations_2 <- subset_white_mediations %>%
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(subset(., select = IBs))) >= 1)

vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_2, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))

```



```{r}
#######  Filter 2:
# Remove individuals with > 5 NA in stressors (retain individuals with at least 45 non-missing values) 
subset_white_mediations_3= subset_white_mediations_2 %>%
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(subset(., select = stress_all_vars))) >= 45)
vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_3, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))

```


```{r}
#######  Filter 3:
# Abuse related variables "17....):
abuse_var= c( "A1SE17E", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17O", "A1SE17I", "A1SE17D", "A1SE17N") 

subset_white_mediations_4 = subset_white_mediations_3  %>%
  filter(
    !(rowSums(is.na(subset(., select = abuse_var))) >= 4) # Minimum= 4. less than that, decreseases the % too much
  )

dim(subset_white_mediations_3)
dim(subset_white_mediations_4)
vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_4, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))

```


```{r}
#######  Filter 4:

# To remove the other 1%, I will select them randomly from people with NA data in those 5 streassors that have > 16%:
str_5=c("A1SE17E", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17O", "A1SE17M")

# 1. Append a helper column counting NAs across str_5
data_miss <- subset_white_mediations_4 %>%
  mutate(miss_str5 = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(str_5)))))

# 2. Find the row-indices of the top most-missing (ties are broken by order in the data)
rows_to_remove <- head(order(data_miss$miss_str5, decreasing = TRUE), 75)

# 3. Slice those rows out, and drop the helper column
subset_white_mediations_5 <- data_miss %>%
  slice(-rows_to_remove) %>%
  dplyr::select(-miss_str5)

dim(subset_white_mediations_4)    
dim(subset_white_mediations_5)    

vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_5, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))
```



```{r}

#######  Filter 5:

#  To remove the other 1% (10 individuals) I will select them randomly from people with NA data in those 5 stressors that have > 18%:
str_x= c("A1SE17M", "A1SE17H", "A1SE17C", "A1SE17I", "A1SE17N")

# 1. Append a helper column counting NAs across str_5
data_miss <- subset_white_mediations_5 %>%
  mutate(miss_str5 = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(str_x)))))

# 2. Find the row-indices of the top most-missing (ties are broken by order in the data)
rows_to_remove <- head(order(data_miss$miss_str5, decreasing = TRUE), 6)

# 3. Slice those rows out, and drop the helper column
subset_white_mediations_6 <- data_miss %>%
  slice(-rows_to_remove) %>%
  dplyr::select(-miss_str5)

dim(subset_white_mediations_5)    
dim(subset_white_mediations_6)    

vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_6, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))


```


## 2) Imputation:

```{r}
### Impute all the variables except by IBs: 

# 1) Exclude IBs from the dataset: 
library(dplyr)

subset_white_to_impute= subset_white_mediations_6[ , !(names(subset_white_mediations_6) %in% IBs)]
str(subset_white_to_impute)

# 2) Split the dataset by sex: 
subset_white_to_impute_M= subset(subset_white_to_impute, C1PRSEX==1)
subset_white_to_impute_F= subset(subset_white_to_impute, C1PRSEX == 2)

nrow(subset_white_to_impute_M)

```


```{r}
###### Impute the data:

### 1) Male group Imputation: 
# Perform multiple imputation:
library(mice)
subset_white_imputed_M <- mice(subset_white_to_impute_M, m = 1, method = 'pmm', maxit = 50, seed = 500)
# Extract the complete dataset:
subset_white_imputed_M_complete <- complete(subset_white_imputed_M)
head(subset_white_imputed_M_complete)

# Visualize the NA data patterns: 
vis_miss(subset_white_imputed_M_complete)


### 2) Female group Imputation: 
subset_white_imputed_F <- mice(subset_white_to_impute_F, m = 1, method = 'pmm', maxit = 50, seed = 500)
# Extract the complete dataset:
subset_white_imputed_F_complete <- complete(subset_white_imputed_F)

# Visualize the NA data patterns: 
vis_miss(subset_white_imputed_F_complete)
```

```{r}
### Re-merge the 2 sex groups:
subset_white_imputed_complete=rbind(subset_white_imputed_F_complete, subset_white_imputed_M_complete)
head(subset_white_imputed_complete)

# Create a dataset with only the IBs: 
vars= c(IBs, "MIDUSID")
IBs_white_df= subset_white_mediations_2[ , (names(subset_white_mediations_2) %in% vars)]
head(IBs_white_df)

# Merge the imputed data with the IBs:
subset_white_imputed_complete_ib= merge(subset_white_imputed_complete, IBs_white_df, by="MIDUSID")
str(subset_white_imputed_complete_ib)
```


```{r}
##### Create the FINAL DATASET for white population using only complete cases: 
complete_cases_white=complete.cases(subset_white_imputed_complete_ib)
sum(complete_cases_white)

# Subset the dataframe to include only complete cases:
subset_white_final_IB = subset_white_imputed_complete_ib[complete_cases_white, ]
str(subset_white_final_IB)
```

```{r}
### Some subset (A) STATS: 

# Age: 
range(subset_white_final_IB$C1PRAGE)
mean(subset_white_final_IB$C1PRAGE)
sd(subset_white_final_IB$C1PRAGE)

# Sex:
# Females % : 
(sum(subset_white_final_IB$C1PRSEX == 2) / sum(!is.na(subset_white_final_IB$C1PRSEX))) * 100

```

#### - Creation of SES variable:

```{r}
# Create the SES using the 2 variables that compound it (Education, household income). The other variable (occupational prestige) was not available for these 2 waves and nothing similar was measured in MIDUS. 

# 1) Adjust income for household size: 
subset_white_final_IB= subset_white_final_IB %>% 
  mutate(adjusted_income = C1STINC / C1PHHSIZE)

# 2) Standardize the variables (z-score):
subset_white_final_IB = subset_white_final_IB %>%
  mutate(
    z_education = scale(C1PB1, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE),
    z_income = scale(adjusted_income, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
  )


# 3) Compute SES as the average of the z-scores:
subset_white_final_IB = subset_white_final_IB %>%
  mutate(SES = (z_education + z_income) / 2)


head(subset_white_final_IB[, c("C1PB1", "C1STINC", "C1PHHSIZE", "adjusted_income", "z_education", "z_income", "SES")])

```

#### -  Filter individuals with 3 Diseases: 

I am removing all individuals with history (diagnosed) of: 
- cancer (current quimiotherapy)
- Parkinson's disease
- other neurological disorder
 

```{r}
ind_diseases= read.csv("../data/individuals_diseases_few.csv")
```



```{r}
# Remove individuals with IDs listed in ind_diseases$diseases
dim(subset_white_final_IB)
subset_white_final_IB<- subset_white_final_IB[!subset_white_final_IB$MIDUSID %in% ind_diseases$diseases,]
dim(subset_white_final_IB)

```

Final N = 276 individuals x 78 columns (subset A)  


```{r}
##### Save this RAW IB dataset (subset A) as .RData: 
save(subset_white_final_IB, file = "../data/subset_white_final_IB.RData")

```
